rationale: F2 (master review 2026-09-30, High): provide()/inject() is Vue's THIRD contract leg — what a component provides and what it depends on — and it had no branch at all. Measured over the restored corpora: `provide(` is written by 34 files, `inject(` by 45, and ZERO corpus files write the Options `provide:` / `inject:` options. Every corpus key is an IDENTIFIER (element-plus writes `provide(anchorKey, …)`, `inject(avatarGroupContextKey, undefined)`), never a string literal — so the key names a declaration this file does not own, which is structurally the F12 shape and gets the same answer: an EDGE to the key, not a copy of its members. Two consequences worth pinning: (a) the value object's keys are this component's own contribution, so `save`/`load` belong to the COMPONENT — before this they surfaced as ownerless methods, indistinguishable in the graph from module-level functions, which the corpus census measured as 4 real rows on element-plus/tour/src/tour.vue; (b) they are ANNOTATED, not duplicated, because the store's symbol key excludes owner and a second symbol at the same name and line silently replaces the first (VSD25). The pre-fix analyzer emits NONE of the edges below and leaves save/load unowned.
